column1: # The independent oracle for the Phase-5 transition relation.
# Authored from `documents/engineering/lift_and_compose_doctrine.md` section 7 — "every
# pair either has a constructor that performs the transition or has no inhabitant at all"
# — read with `substrate_doctrine.md` section 4, which is where the shape of the layer
# stack comes from: a host synthesizes a Linux frame, and that frame runs a container.
# Nothing below is read off the implementation, which is what lets this table stay red
# when the relation is wrong.
# Three rules decide every row, and each is stated once here rather than nine times below:
#   outward     a transition moves one layer outward, so `on-host -> in-frame` and
#               `in-frame -> in-container` have constructors
#   no descent  nothing moves inward. An effect confined by a frame cannot reach the host
#               that provides it — that confinement is what the frame is for — so the
#               three inward pairs have no inhabitant
#   no skipping `on-host -> in-container` has no inhabitant either. Reaching a container
#               from the host is two moves, and saying so is what composition is for; a
#               relation that closed under transitivity would erase the distinction
# The three reflexive pairs are admitted, because an effect that has not moved is still
# somewhere and a relation with no identity is not one a path can be built over. They take
# a witness like every other transition.
# The gate joins this table to `admits` in both directions: a pair the table admits and
# the relation refuses fails, and so does a pair the relation admits and the table does
# not. The nine rows are every ordered pair of the closed three-member set, so a tenth row
# names a layer that does not exist and a missing row is a pair nothing decided.
# source<TAB>target<TAB>admitted<TAB>why
